readings.meaning: cut screen time or time spent

ambiguity: Could be read as a UI sort control (sort by time or age) rather than reducing duration, or confused with a plain hourglass at very small sizes.

modifier_semantics.meaning: decrease, reduce, count down, or descending order

example_tasks.task: Trim the conference talk rehearsal down from 35 minutes to under 25
Get cold boot time on the media server under twenty seconds
Shave ten minutes off the morning school drop-off routine before winter
Cut the weekly all-hands from an hour to 30 minutes
Bring average ticket first-response wait time below four hours
Switch to 25-minute defaults in Google Calendar
Cut the webpack production bundle build from eight minutes down to under two
Get my Rubik's cube average solve time under forty-five seconds before the meetup
Reduce evening Doomscrolling on Instagram and Reddit to thirty minutes max per day

example_tasks_es: Reducir el tiempo de pantalla diario en el móvil a menos de una hora
Acortar la reunión diaria del equipo a quince minutos
Bajar mi tiempo de 10k por debajo de cincuenta minutos
example_tasks_ru: Сократить экранное время на телефоне до часа в день
Уменьшить время сборки проекта в CI до трех минут
Урезать утреннюю планерку с получаса до пятнадцати минут

context_tasks.task: Prep dough the night before so breakfast takes less time
Turn off phone notifications during deep work blocks
Buy a pressure cooker to speed up weeknight stews
Delete TikTok from iPad for a month

near_misses.task: Buy a 3-minute brass sand timer for brewing tea
near_misses.better: plain hourglass or tea icon (no downward arrow modifier)

near_misses.task: Check how much time is left on the parking meter
Buy blue-light glasses for late coding sessions
near_misses.better: glasses icon (even if under a 'Screen Time' project)

near_misses.task: Extend the library book loan for another two weeks
near_misses.better: book icon or hourglass with upward/plus modifier

reasoning: The icon clearly combines an hourglass (time/duration) with a downward arrow (decrease/reduce or countdown). While it also resembles a 'sort by duration' UI button, it fits a real niche of personal and work tasks focused on reducing screen time, shortening meeting lengths, or cutting down build and wait times.
